operations.summary: Old release targeted update of legacy_name for one profile id.
New release targeted update of display_name for one profile id.
Selects profiles WHERE display_name IS NULL then per-row conditional backfill SET display_name=legacy_name WHERE display_name IS NULL.

conflicts.risk_explanation: Backfill SELECTs rows WHERE display_name IS NULL then later UPDATEs SET display_name WHERE display_name IS NULL. Concurrent v2 UPDATE sets display_name directly. Without the IS NULL guard the backfill would overwrite the user's new display value with stale legacy_name (lost update). Test verifies guard holds under all interleavings.

Backfill reads legacy_name in one transaction then copies it to display_name in a later per-row transaction. Concurrent v1 UPDATE changes legacy_name between SELECT and UPDATE, so backfill copies a stale value. Already-backfilled rows are never repaired, so new-reader view diverges from final legacy_name.

Rolling deployment dual-write divergence: v1 writes only legacy_name, v2 writes only display_name with no trigger or app-level sync. v1 updates are invisible to new-code readers of display_name and v2 updates invisible to old-code readers of legacy_name. Concurrent per-column UPDATEs must at least not clobber each other at row level.

tests.name: backfill_vs_display_update
tests.rationale: Same NULL row raced by backfill and v2 display write. Correct code leaves v2 value in place in every order due to WHERE display_name IS NULL. Missing guard would lose v2 update when SELECT precedes v2 and UPDATE follows it.

invariants.description: concurrent v2 display value must survive; backfill must not overwrite non-NULL display
neither backfill nor v2 modifies legacy_name

tests.name: rolling_three_way_backfill_v1_v2
tests.rationale: Old release, new release and backfill job on same NULL row simultaneously. Checks full rolling hazard: legacy update not lost, display update not lost to backfill, and per-column updates coexist. Any full-row overwrite or unconditional backfill would violate one invariant.

invariants.description: only v1 writes legacy_name so final must be v1 value
v2 display must win over backfill copy in every order due to conditional backfill

tests.name: dual_column_isolation_v1_v2
tests.rationale: Concurrent old-release and new-release updates to different columns of same already-backfilled row. Targeted UPDATEs must preserve each other; read-modify-write of whole row would lose one column. Also exposes logical divergence from missing dual-write sync.

invariants.description: v2 column update must persist alongside v1

tests.name: backfill_vs_legacy_update
tests.rationale: Backfill non-atomic copy raced with v1 legacy update. Legacy must not be lost. Display must become populated from legacy, but may be stale (pre-update orig) if v1 commits between backfill SELECT and UPDATE, illustrating stale-read hazard and post-backfill divergence.

invariants.description: backfill never writes legacy_name so v1 value must remain
backfill must populate display from some observed legacy value, never NULL or corrupt
